penalties_description: FIRS/NRS will invoke mutual administrative assistance instruments to enforce, collect and recover VAT from non-resident suppliers that fail to account for or remit VAT due. Failure to register incurs penalties. The NRS may appoint collection agents including digital platforms and payment processors.
verbatim_quote: Intermediary platforms will be viewed as deemed sellers responsible for registering, invoicing, collecting and remitting VAT on sales completed through their platforms.
notes: Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (NTA 2025) delayed full non-resident obligations to 1 January 2026. Digital services rules under simplified compliance regime were effective from 1 January 2022; goods from 1 January 2024. The USD 25,000 threshold applies to non-resident providers' annual turnover from Nigeria. The NGN 25,000,000 threshold applies to domestic resident registration. Marketplace/platform deemed supplier rules exist but are framed as a discretionary designation: the NRS 'may appoint' platforms as collection agents rather than an automatic deemed-supplier mandate. B2B reverse charge also applies so that non-resident suppliers do not charge VAT to Nigerian business customers. A Simplified Compliance Regime portal is being rolled out for non-resident registration and reporting.
